title: Unbounded descent criterion with local cohomology bounds
statement: Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),R)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], with commutative ring sheaves on sites small relative to the universe of their module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], [def-weil-size-convention]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal A\subset\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and $\mathcal B\subset\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ be weak Serre subcategories: each is strictly full, contains zero, and is closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between its objects and under extensions. Write $D_{\mathcal A}$ and $D_{\mathcal B}$ for the full subcategories of objects all of whose cohomology sheaves belong to the indicated subcategory. Suppose (1) module pullback $f^*$ is exact; (2) $f^*$ restricts to an equivalence $\mathcal B\simeq\mathcal A$ with quasi-inverse $f_*$; (3) the canonical derived unit $G\to Rf_*f^*G$ is an isomorphism for every $G\in\mathcal B$ placed in degree zero. Suppose further that each of $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O,\mathcal A)$ and $(\mathcal D,R,\mathcal B)$ has the following local bound property: there is a set $\mathcal V$ of objects such that every site object has a covering by members of $\mathcal V$, and for each $V\in\mathcal V$ there are an integer $d_V$ and a cofinal collection of covering families $\{V_i\to V\}$ for which $H^p(V_i,F)=0$ for every $p>d_V$ and every module $F$ in the indicated subcategory. Here cohomology is the right derived functor of sections. Then $Lf^*=f^*$ and $Rf_*$ restrict to mutually quasi-inverse triangulated equivalences $D_{\mathcal B}(R)\simeq D_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal O)$, and the canonical derived adjunction unit and counit are isomorphisms on these subcategories.

proof.text: Exactness and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identify $Lf^*$ with termwise $f^*$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $H^jf^*K=f^*H^jK$, so $f^*$ maps $D_{\mathcal B}$ into $D_{\mathcal A}$. It commutes naturally with good truncation [def-kun-truncations]: exactness preserves its defining kernels and cokernels, and the comparison intertwines the truncation maps.

For $F\in\mathcal A$, choose $G\in\mathcal B$ and an isomorphism $F\cong f^*G$. Hypothesis (3) gives $Rf_*F\cong Rf_*f^*G\cong G[0]$. Hence $R^pf_*F=0$ for $p>0$ and $f_*F\cong G\in\mathcal B$. The three hypotheses of [lem-sfb-ringed-bounded-below-descent-criterion] hold, giving the canonical unit and counit isomorphisms on the bounded-below categories.

Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-local-bound-direct-image-truncation] with $N=0$: step 2 checks its higher-image hypotheses, and both local bound properties are hypotheses of the item. Thus $Rf_*$ maps $D_{\mathcal A}$ into $D_{\mathcal B}$, and for $j\geq-n$ the canonical map $H^j(Rf_*K)\to H^j(Rf_*\tau_{\geq-n}K)$ is invertible.

Let $K'\in D_{\mathcal B}$, fix $j$, and choose $n\geq0$ with $j\geq-n$. Naturality of the unit gives the square from $K'\to Rf_*f^*K'$ to $\tau_{\geq-n}K'\to Rf_*f^*\tau_{\geq-n}K'$. On $H^j$ its left vertical arrow is invertible by truncation, its right vertical arrow by step 3 and step 1's truncation comparison, and its bottom arrow by the bounded-below criterion. Hence $H^j$ of the top unit is invertible. As $j$ was arbitrary the unit is an isomorphism.

For $K\in D_{\mathcal A}$ choose $j,n$ as above. Naturality of the counit gives the square from $f^*Rf_*K\to K$ to $f^*Rf_*\tau_{\geq-n}K\to\tau_{\geq-n}K$. Its right vertical arrow is invertible on $H^j$ by truncation. Its left vertical arrow is invertible on $H^j$ by step 3 and $H^jf^*(-)=f^*H^j(-)$. The bottom counit is invertible by the bounded-below criterion. Thus the top counit is invertible on every cohomology sheaf and hence is an isomorphism.

The weak Serre hypotheses give the inherited triangulated subcategories by [lem-sbc-cohomology-in-weak-serre-subcategory]. Step 1's factorization is triangulated. Module sheaves on these small ringed sites have K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], so [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] makes $Rf_*$ triangulated as well. The canonical unbounded ringed adjunction is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. It restricts, since both functors preserve the specified subcategories. Its unit and counit, proved invertible above, exhibit the asserted mutually quasi-inverse triangulated equivalences.
